notes: JAMB Government 2020 — 100 questions compiled from verified sources + style-matched items. Not official JAMB papers.

questions.prompt: A constitution is a legal document?
options: For mobilising people for political action
Forming the basis upon which a government rules the country
That is only useful in a democracy
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental legal framework that establishes the principles, institutions, and rules for governance.

questions.prompt: A government in which control of ultimate power is by a few who rule in their selfish interest is classified as?
questions.explanation: Oligarchy is a system where a small group holds power, often using it for personal gain rather than public good.

questions.prompt: The judicial organ of government is the body which?
questions.explanation: The judiciary is the branch of government responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice.

questions.prompt: A set of internalized norms which guides political action is called?
questions.explanation: Ideology refers to a coherent set of beliefs and values that shape political behaviour and policy preferences.

questions.prompt: A characteristic feature of communism is?
questions.explanation: Communism typically involves centralized control, often through a single-party dictatorship, with limited individual freedoms.

questions.prompt: In a democracy, sovereignty is in?
questions.explanation: In a democracy, ultimate authority (sovereignty) resides with the people, who exercise it directly or through representatives.

questions.prompt: A bill that applies to the whole population and is intended to promote the general welfare is called?
questions.explanation: A public bill affects the general public and addresses matters of broad national or societal interest.

questions.prompt: Fascism developed in?
questions.explanation: Fascism as a political ideology first emerged in Italy under Benito Mussolini in the early 20th century.

questions.prompt: The theory of separation of powers was first clearly formulated by?
questions.explanation: Montesquieu articulated the doctrine of separation of powers in his work The Spirit of the Laws.

questions.prompt: When a state is subject to no other authority, it is said to be?
questions.explanation: Sovereignty is the supreme authority of a state to govern itself without external interference.

questions.prompt: Government by the wealthy is known as?
questions.explanation: Plutocracy is a system of governance where the wealthy class holds power and influence.

questions.prompt: A system of government in which the same person is both head of state and head of government is?
questions.explanation: In a presidential system, the president serves as both head of state and head of government, combining ceremonial and executive functions.

questions.prompt: The process by which a country gains the right to govern itself is called?
questions.explanation: Independence is the acquisition of self-governance and freedom from external control.

questions.prompt: A political system in which power is shared between a central government and constituent units is?
questions.explanation: Federalism divides power between a central authority and regional governments, each with defined spheres of jurisdiction.

questions.prompt: The principle that the law is supreme and applies equally to all citizens is called?
questions.explanation: The rule of law ensures that no one is above the law and that legal processes govern all actions.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was not established by the 1979 Nigerian constitution?
questions.explanation: The National Population Commission was not created by the 1979 Constitution; other bodies were established under different legal instruments.

questions.prompt: A good example of a confederal state is?
questions.explanation: ECOWAS exemplifies a confederation of independent states that cooperate under a limited central authority while retaining their sovereignty.

questions.prompt: The type of government operated in Nigeria between October 1st 1979 and December 31st 1983 was?
questions.explanation: Nigeria operated a presidential system during the Second Republic (1979–1983), with an executive president.

questions.prompt: A unitary system of government is characterized by?
options: Concentration of power at the centre
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, the central government holds supreme authority, and local governments derive their powers from it.

questions.prompt: A parliamentary system is one in which the executive is?
options: Drawn from and accountable to the legislature
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the prime minister and cabinet are members of the legislature and remain in office only with its confidence.

questions.prompt: An absolute monarchy is one in which the monarch?
questions.explanation: In an absolute monarchy, the monarch wields unconstrained authority, often claiming divine right.

questions.prompt: A republican form of government is one in which?
options: The head of state is elected
questions.explanation: Republics have an elected or appointed head of state rather than a hereditary monarch.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes a totalitarian regime?
options: Extensive state control over public and private life
questions.explanation: Totalitarian regimes seek to control virtually all aspects of society, suppressing dissent and independent institutions.

questions.prompt: A theocracy is a system of government in which?
questions.explanation: In a theocracy, religious authority is the basis of political rule, and religious law often serves as state law.

questions.prompt: Anarchy is best defined as?
questions.explanation: Anarchy refers to a condition of lawlessness and absence of effective governmental authority.

questions.prompt: The first Nigerian constitution to provide for the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy was the?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy as a guide for governance.

questions.prompt: The charter of the United Nations was drawn up in?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945, establishing the United Nations.

questions.prompt: The idea of making the civil service permanent, neutral, and anonymous is to?
options: Make civil servants a functional elite
questions.explanation: Permanence, neutrality, and anonymity protect civil servants from political interference and promote professional efficiency.

questions.prompt: The delineation of constituencies is a major duty of the?
questions.explanation: Electoral commissions are responsible for dividing the country into constituencies for representative purposes.

questions.prompt: A major issue that distinguishes pressure groups from political parties is?
options: They both seek to capture political power
Pressure groups seek to influence policy, while parties seek to form government
Pressure groups are larger than parties
questions.explanation: Pressure groups aim to influence government decisions without seeking to govern directly, whereas political parties contest elections to form government.

questions.prompt: The Ibadan Conference of 1950 was convened to discuss the provisions of the?
questions.explanation: The Ibadan Conference was held to deliberate on the Macpherson Constitution before its enactment.

questions.prompt: Nigeria’s head of government in 1963 was?
questions.explanation: Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa served as Prime Minister (head of government) in 1963, while Nnamdi Azikiwe was President (ceremonial head of state).

questions.prompt: A constitution that is difficult to amend is said to be?
questions.explanation: Rigid constitutions require special procedures, such as supermajorities or referendums, for amendment.

questions.prompt: The process of amending a constitution is called?
questions.explanation: Constitutional amendment is the formal procedure for altering the provisions of a constitution.

questions.prompt: A written constitution is one that is?
questions.explanation: A written constitution consolidates the fundamental rules of governance into a formal, codified document.

questions.prompt: The doctrine of judicial review allows courts to?
questions.explanation: Judicial review empowers courts to review and invalidate legislative or executive actions that violate the constitution.

questions.prompt: A federal constitution typically provides for?
options: Division of powers between central and regional governments
questions.explanation: Federal constitutions distribute authority between a central government and constituent units, each with defined powers.

questions.prompt: The concept of “constitutionalism” implies?
questions.explanation: Constitutionalism is the principle that governmental power should be legally limited and constrained by a constitution.

questions.prompt: An unwritten constitution is found in?
questions.explanation: The UK has an uncodified constitution derived from statutes, conventions, and judicial decisions.

questions.prompt: A constitution that can be amended by ordinary legislative process is?
questions.explanation: Flexible constitutions can be amended through the same procedure as ordinary laws.

questions.prompt: The simple plurality electoral system is often criticized because?
options: The ruling party may lose the election
The winner may not poll an absolute majority
It works against all opposition parties
questions.explanation: Under plurality voting, a candidate can win with fewer than 50% of votes cast if they have the largest single share, potentially lacking majority support.

questions.prompt: One of the duties of the legislature is to?
questions.explanation: The primary function of the legislature is lawmaking, alongside representation and oversight.

questions.prompt: The highest court in Nigeria before 1963 was the?
options: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
questions.explanation: Before Nigeria became a republic in 1963, final appeals went to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London.

questions.prompt: Rates are generally collected in Nigeria by?
questions.explanation: Local government councils are constitutionally empowered to collect rates and levies within their jurisdictions.

questions.prompt: The main function of the Code of Conduct Bureau is to?
options: Give the police more powers to make arrests
Give the judiciary more powers to discipline erring judges
Protect public officers from the press
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau enforces ethical standards and asset declaration rules for public officers to promote accountability.

questions.prompt: A common feature of government is?
questions.explanation: All governments engage in making and implementing public policy, even if other features vary.

questions.prompt: The independent National Electoral Commission has the power to prepare and maintain the register of?
questions.explanation: INEC is responsible for compiling and updating the voter register for elections.

questions.prompt: The process of manipulating constituency boundaries to favour a particular party is called?
questions.explanation: Gerrymandering is the deliberate manipulation of electoral boundaries for partisan advantage.

questions.prompt: The legislature performs oversight functions primarily through?
questions.explanation: Legislative oversight involves scrutinizing executive actions through committees, hearings, and approval of budgets and appointments.

questions.prompt: The executive arm of government is responsible for?
questions.explanation: The executive implements laws, formulates policies, and administers public affairs.

questions.prompt: The judiciary is independent when?
options: It is funded by the executive
Judges are appointed by the president without oversight
It is free from external influence in its decisions
It takes directives from the legislature【generated】
questions.explanation: Judicial independence requires that courts decide cases impartially, free from political or other improper influence.

questions.prompt: A civil service is described as anonymous because?
options: Civil servants are unknown to the public
Individual civil servants are not personally credited or blamed for official actions
questions.explanation: Anonymity means civil servants work behind the scenes, with actions attributed to the government or department rather than individuals.

questions.prompt: The permanent secretary in a ministry is?
options: The administrative head of the ministry
questions.explanation: The permanent secretary is the senior civil servant who heads the administrative machinery of a ministry.

questions.prompt: The principle of collective responsibility applies to?
options: The cabinet in a parliamentary system
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary cabinet, ministers are collectively responsible for government decisions and must publicly support them or resign.

questions.prompt: The head of the civil service in Nigeria is the?
options: Secretary to the Government of the Federation
questions.explanation: The Head of the Civil Service is the most senior civil servant responsible for coordinating the service.

questions.prompt: Nigeria’s non-aligned policy means that she will?
options: Have nothing to do with the superpowers
Not take sides in international issues based on ideological considerations
Avoid having any dealing with any country with ideological leanings
Relate only with member countries of the Non-Aligned Movement
questions.explanation: Non-alignment means Nigeria avoids committing to either Cold War bloc and makes decisions based on national interests.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was the last to win independence from colonial rule?
questions.explanation: Angola gained independence from Portugal in 1975, later than the other listed countries.

questions.prompt: Who reorganised Nigeria’s four regions into twelve states in May 1967?
questions.explanation: General Gowon created 12 states in 1967 to reduce regional tensions and strengthen central authority.

questions.prompt: The absence of the rule of law in government will bring about?
questions.explanation: Without the rule of law, arbitrary exercise of power can lead to rights violations and abuse.

questions.prompt: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the?
questions.explanation: The Privy Council in London served as the final appellate court for Nigeria before the 1963 republican constitution.

questions.prompt: The first Nigerian constitution to provide for the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy was the?
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced these principles as a guide for public policy and governance.

questions.prompt: Under the 1999 Constitution, the power to create local governments is vested in the?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution empowers State Houses of Assembly to create and abolish local government areas.

questions.prompt: A major issue that distinguishes pressure groups from political parties is that pressure groups?
options: Seek to influence policy rather than capture power
questions.explanation: Pressure groups aim to influence government decisions without seeking to govern directly, unlike political parties.

questions.prompt: Nigeria’s federal system is characterized by?
options: Division of powers between federal and state governments
questions.explanation: Federalism in Nigeria divides authority between the federal government and state governments, with local governments as a third tier.

questions.prompt: The federal capital territory of Nigeria is?
questions.explanation: Abuja became Nigeria’s federal capital in 1991, replacing Lagos.

questions.prompt: The 1963 Republican Constitution made Nigeria a?
questions.explanation: The 1963 Constitution abolished the Queen as head of state and established a Nigerian president as ceremonial head of state.

questions.prompt: The concept of “federal character” in Nigeria is intended to?
options: Ensure equitable representation of diverse groups in national institutions
questions.explanation: Federal character aims to reflect Nigeria’s ethnic and regional diversity in appointments and distribution of resources.

questions.prompt: The exclusive legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Exclusive legislative list items are reserved for the federal legislature alone.

questions.prompt: The concurrent legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Concurrent list items allow both federal and state legislatures to make laws, with federal law prevailing in case of conflict.

questions.prompt: The residuary legislative list contains matters on which?
options: Only the federal government can legislate
Both federal and state governments can legislate
questions.explanation: Residuary matters are those not explicitly assigned, often left to state governments in a federal system.

questions.prompt: The Nigerian judiciary has how many tiers?
questions.explanation: Nigeria’s judiciary has the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, and High Courts (federal and state), plus lower courts, forming a three-tier appellate structure.

questions.prompt: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is headed by the?
options: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of Nigeria is the highest judicial officer and heads the Supreme Court.

questions.prompt: The Court of Appeal is headed by the?
options: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: The President of the Court of Appeal heads that court and is second in judicial hierarchy.

questions.prompt: The process of removing a judge for misconduct is called?
questions.explanation: Impeachment is the formal constitutional process for removing senior public officials, including judges, for misconduct.

questions.prompt: The Attorney-General of the Federation is the?
options: Chief law officer of the federal government
Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The Attorney-General is the chief legal adviser and prosecutor for the federal government.

questions.prompt: The first political party in Nigeria was the?
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)【generated】
questions.explanation: The NNDP, founded by Herbert Macaulay in 1923, was Nigeria’s first political party.

questions.prompt: A political party is best defined as?
options: A group of people with common interests seeking to influence policy
An organized group that seeks to capture and exercise political power
questions.explanation: Political parties are organized groups that contest elections to gain control of government.

questions.prompt: The primary function of a political party is to?
options: Advocate for specific interest groups only
questions.explanation: Political parties aggregate interests, contest elections, and organize government when victorious.

questions.prompt: The type of electoral system used in Nigeria is?
questions.explanation: Nigeria generally uses the first-past-the-post/plurality system in single-member constituencies.

questions.prompt: A general election is one in which?
options: All or most constituencies elect representatives
questions.explanation: General elections involve nationwide voting to elect representatives at various levels.

questions.prompt: A by-election is held to?
options: Fill a vacant seat between general elections
questions.explanation: By-elections are held to fill casual vacancies arising between general elections.

questions.prompt: A referendum is a process in which?
options: Citizens vote directly on a specific issue or policy
questions.explanation: A referendum allows the electorate to approve or reject a specific proposal directly.

questions.prompt: The right to vote is known as?
questions.explanation: The franchise (or suffrage) is the legal right to vote in political elections.

questions.prompt: An electoral malpractices includes?
questions.explanation: Ballot stuffing is a form of electoral fraud where illegitimate votes are added to the count.

questions.prompt: A pressure group that seeks to promote the interests of workers is a?
questions.explanation: Trade unions are pressure groups that represent and protect the interests of workers.

questions.prompt: The Nigerian Labour Congress (NLC) is an example of a?
questions.explanation: The NLC is a federation of trade unions that acts as a pressure group on labour and economic issues.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a pressure group?
questions.explanation: The NBA is a professional association that advocates for legal professionals and justice-related issues.

questions.prompt: A political party that is dominant in a political system is called a?
questions.explanation: The ruling party is the party that holds governmental power after winning elections.

questions.prompt: The opposition party in a democracy is important because it?
options: Checks the excesses of the ruling party
questions.explanation: Opposition parties provide alternative policies and hold the government accountable.

questions.prompt: A coalition government is formed when?
options: One party wins an outright majority
Two or more parties combine to form a government
questions.explanation: Coalition governments arise when no single party has a majority, prompting parties to cooperate.

questions.prompt: The charter of the United Nations was drawn up in?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter was adopted and signed in San Francisco in 1945.

questions.prompt: The founder of the Universal Negro Improvement Association was?
questions.explanation: Marcus Garvey founded the UNIA in 1914 to promote Black nationalism and Pan-Africanism.

questions.prompt: ECOWAS was established in?
questions.explanation: The Economic Community of West African States was founded in 1975 through the Treaty of Lagos.

questions.prompt: The headquarters of ECOWAS is located in?
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission is headquartered in Abuja, Nigeria.

questions.prompt: The main problem of ECOWAS is lack of?
questions.explanation: A recurring challenge for ECOWAS has been inadequate political will among member states to implement collective decisions.

questions.prompt: Nigeria became a member of OPEC in?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries in 1971.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a founding member of OPEC?
questions.explanation: Venezuela was one of the five founding members of OPEC in 1960.

questions.prompt: The African Union (AU) was established in?
questions.explanation: The AU was formally launched in 2002, succeeding the Organization of African Unity (OAU).

questions.prompt: The headquarters of the African Union is in?
questions.explanation: The AU headquarters is located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.prompt: The United Nations Security Council has how many permanent members?
questions.explanation: The five permanent members are China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
